newsitem.title: USA: ACE Lloyd's agencies have $1.2 bln capacity.
newsitem.headline: ACE Lloyd's agencies have $1.2 bln capacity.

text.p: ACE Ltd said its three managing agencies at Lloyd's of London have total capacity of $1.2 billion, or 745 million stg, for 1997.

Of that capacity, $225 million, or 142 million stg, will come from ACE Capital and the remainder will come from other investors, ACE chief financial officer Christopher Marshall told a New York Society of Security Analysts insurance conference.
ACE Capital provided capacity of just 25 million stg in 1996, he said.
Although, ACE will provide capacity of 142 million stg in 1997, he said only about 50-60 percent of that will translate into net premiums written on ACE's income statement.

However, because ACE's fiscal year ends September 30 and its Lloyd's participation is booked one quarter in arrears, only 50 percent of its 1997 Lloyd's participation will be recorded in ACE's fiscal 1997, Marshall said.
Marshall said ACE's Methuen managing agency has capacity of 384 million stg for 1997 and its ACE London Aviation managing agency has 1997 capacity of 204 million stg.
ACE London Underwriting has 1997 capacity of 157 million stg, he said.
Marshall said the participation in Lloyd's is becoming a major part of ACE's operations.
Marshall also told the conference that Ace was one of the insurers of AT&T Corp's Telstar 401 satellite, which stopped operating earlier this month.
However, he said the loss on the satellite "won't impact our results for the March quarter."
Marshall also said ACE has not made any further additions to its reserves for losses on breast implant litigation.
In 1994, ACE said it took a $200 million charge to earnings as a result of increases to reserves for breast implant litigation losses.
